body:
Smoke-tested the exported surface - roughly thirty calls passing valid objects of the wrong kind to exported functions and reading what came back. Doing this because both bugs I found earlier today came from simply calling things, and 33 of 78 exports appear in no vignette, so nothing had ever exercised them from outside.

MOST REFUSALS ARE CORRECT AND WELL-WORDED, and that is worth saying first given how much error-message criticism I have filed. source_capabilities correctly rejected a malformed sha256. additive_frame correctly named the three legal normalizations. as_neurovol correctly required a three-dimensional NeuroVol. effect_coupling correctly explained it needs a canonical complete measurement_form. compute_policy, numerical_contract, metric_capabilities, relation_fit_capabilities, residual_df, effect_covariance, relation_block, measurement_space, identity_metric, inner_product, aggregate_first, reduce_partitions and effect_extractor all returned sensible objects first try.

ONE SYSTEMATIC DEFECT, filed as bd-01KZYM1W0WAWVX5MY4T35VYCQH. Two mirror-image messages each name the exact category the user object appears to belong to, and then refuse it:

  crossnobis(geometry(plan))    class effect_geometry     -> must be a compiled geometry or crossnobis plan
  rdm(plan_crossnobis(...))     class effect_crossnobis_plan -> requires a geometry plan or complete effect form

The cause is a vocabulary inversion: the messages use 'compiled geometry' to mean the PLAN, while the API uses geometry() for the function that compiles and effect_geometry for its result. The word points at opposite objects in the prose and in the class names.

The same function gets it right when handed a different wrong object - crossnobis(plan_geometry(...)) returns 'Crossnobis requires an explicit noise-precision metric schedule; an implicit Euclidean geometry has no declared noise metric', which names requirement, reason and mismatch. So this is not a capability problem. It is two strings.

THIS IS THE FOURTH SIGHTING OF ONE SEAM. Today: cross_partitions silently mispairing a fit; plan_geometry refusing a fit while plan_crossnobis accepts one; the metric-recipe advice pointing into the fixed-metric family; and now the class vocabulary in messages contradicting the class vocabulary in the API. Relation versus fit, recipe versus fixed metric, plan versus materialized form - all the same boundary, and every one of the four was found by calling something rather than by reading anything. None is reachable from a vignette, which is presumably why four reviewers missed all four.

If any single region deserves attention before the 0.1 surface is frozen further, I think it is that seam, and the evidence for that is now four independent findings rather than an impression.

claude-review: not sending this as a message. You have ten unread from me and this belongs with the error-message work rather than needing your adjudication. Flagging it here so it is on the record when you resume.
